decisions.title: Acceptance criteria and definition-of-done stay advisory at task completion, but completion must report unresolved items
decisions.context: Opened by an inbound report from quest-web (via the orchestrator): a task with one unchecked acceptance criterion completed silently -- exit 0, no warning, nothing in the record. A second, independent incident on 2026-09-13 (another fleet session) closed two tasks with 0 of 3 criteria checked, via the older 1-based --check-ac numbering trap (QCLI-269) whose usage errors went unseen. QCLI-252's own investigation found zero enforcement anywhere in src/ tying acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone to the completion transition (only gates/gateEvents block, a structurally separate field), and confirmed command-help.ts and the task-finalization guide never said so plainly.
decisions.outcome: Kept advisory, but stopped being silent: quest task complete now computes an additive unresolvedAtCompletion field (acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone unchecked items, index+text) on its JSON result -- present only when something is unresolved, matching this codebase's omit-when-empty convention -- and prints a stderr line prefixed Warning: naming the unresolved items. Exit code and the completed record's own fields are unchanged; opum-cli-e2e's contract check.stderrSilentOnSuccess already tolerates a warning-prefixed line on success, so this does not read as a failure to any known consumer. command-help.ts's task complete summary and the task-finalization guide now state this plainly. Scoped to task complete only (not archive/pause/start/demote), since completion is the one transition where whether the work was actually finished is the live question.
